title: Can I feel pregnant when my wife is?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss Couvade syndrome (sympathetic or phantom pregnancy), in which a man, usually an expectant father, develops pregnancy symptoms such as a swollen belly, cravings, and mood changes while his wife is pregnant. They cover its psychosomatic nature, the theory of rivalry or emotional attachment, that women can also experience it after miscarriage or loss, and the case of Lisa Montgomery, who murdered a pregnant woman in December 2004 and removed the unborn child. They note the medical community has not established a clear cause, mention possible links to hormones, and suggest counseling and talking with a partner as help. The episode opens with a brief intro and closes with a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Couvade syndrome
segments.summary: Josh introduces the question of whether a man can feel pregnant when his wife is, and states that couvade, also called false or sympathetic pregnancy, is described by anecdotal evidence and was first noted by Hippocrates. He describes the phantom belly and cravings.

segments.title: Causes and rivalry theory
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the condition is psychosomatic and linked to emotional attachment or confusion during pregnancy changes, with one theory being rivalry with the wife for attention. They note it also affects women after a miscarriage or child loss.

segments.title: Bloody Mary and Lisa Montgomery cases
segments.summary: Josh mentions Bloody Mary and says she may have had this syndrome. They discuss how women with the condition can face more serious consequences because they expect to give birth, and describe Lisa Montgomery, who in December 2004 murdered a pregnant woman and removed her unborn child.

segments.title: Medical understanding and treatment
segments.summary: The hosts describe the condition as a mental disorder affecting the body and note the medical community has not established a clear link, though research into hormones is ongoing. They discuss media depictions on Grey's Anatomy and Law & Order: SVU, and that counseling and talking with a partner can help.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up by advising those with couvade to seek help and be sensitive to others, point listeners to the article Can I feel pregnant when my wife is, and close with the show's sign-off and a request for listener feedback.
